prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of the incretin hormone GLP-1 and its active forms that made incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: The round-1 exchange did not change my lead. All six of us put B046 first, and I keep testing that against the content, not the count. The chain from proglucagon processing, through the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide and its glucose-dependent insulinotropic action, to central and gastric effects is complete. It has been confirmed independently for decades, and large outcome trials now show glycaemic, weight, cardiovascular and renal benefit. Maturity is not in question. Holst (secretion and physiology), Drucker (mechanism and translational proof of concept) and Mojsov (identification and synthesis of the active peptide) cover the discovery side of the line, and I accept the chair's wording that the citation should name physiology and active forms and not claim the drug-design step. I do not add a second part. Of the candidates for one, B040 would need Eshhar to be clean, and a second part would force a cut to the GLP-1 trio under the three-person cap, which would damage the stronger achievement.
statement.case_against: Attribution remains the weakness and I cannot close it from the supplied record. Mojsov's priority against Habener's group is contested, and Habener and the early proglucagon sequencing groups are outside the credited names. Excluding Knudsen can be read as honouring physiology while skipping the step that produced the medicine. I treat that as a real cost of the configuration. I judge it smaller than the cost of crediting an optimisation step as a discovery, or of dropping Mojsov and losing the first link, the active peptide. A citation worded around physiology will not satisfy a reader who thinks the drugs are the discovery.

responses.point: If the committee treats the industrial step as essential, she would swap Mojsov for Knudsen, which removes the priority dispute but loses the peptide identification. She prefers to keep the arc and describe the therapies in the citation.
responses.response: I agree with keeping the arc, and I think your swap shows the cost clearly. Replacing Mojsov with Knudsen makes the priority argument disappear only by changing the achievement from physiology to physiology plus development, and then the identification of the active peptide has no credited owner. I also accept your point that the contested priority is a reason for careful wording, not a reason to drop her. Where I move slightly is on the fallback: if Mojsov's credit proved unworkable, I would sooner go to Holst and Drucker alone, as Linnarsson suggests, than to a Knudsen swap, because it keeps the claim to physiology intact.

responses.point: He would treat Habener as a limit of the supplied credit and not a reason to hold back the prize, would word the citation around physiology and active forms, and would support recording Habener's role in deliberations.
responses.response: I agree on both points. We can only award credited names, so the honest course is to word the citation so that it claims no sole priority, and to record in our deliberations that Habener and the proglucagon sequencing groups sit outside the supplied credit. I support that record. It does not change my configuration, because it limits what we can say, not whether the physiology is established. I also accept your position that Knudsen should enter only in a two-part prize pairing physiology with a development achievement, and I do not think that is needed. I had floated the Knudsen swap in round 1 only as an alternative reading, and I now think it is the weaker one.

responses.point: He would keep Mojsov in because without the identification and synthesis of the active peptide the physiology and drug story lose their first link, with Holst and Drucker alone as a thinner fallback. He also accepts the two-person June and Sadelain reading of B040.
responses.response: I agree that Mojsov's identification and synthesis of the active peptide is the link that connects Holst's secretion work to the receptor biology and the drugs, so I keep her in. I am glad we now agree on B040: costimulated CAR design and CD19 clinical translation belong to June and Sadelain, and Rosenberg's adoptive transfer is a forerunner. Your fallback of Holst and Drucker is what I would use if the priority question became decisive, but I would not start from it, because that reading assigns the active-peptide step to nobody, which is a thinner claim than the record supports.

responses.point: He supports the June and Sadelain pair but ranks B040 only as the strongest alternative because Eshhar's original chimeric receptor is outside the credited names, a gap he would not accept lightly. He also wants a citation that does not claim the drug-design step.
responses.response: The Eshhar gap is the reason I do not argue for B040 as a second part, and I have moved toward your reading. In round 1 I treated June and Sadelain as the cleaner pair, but cleaner among CAR-T options is not the same as complete, and a prize that skips the original chimeric receptor concept is open to the same priority criticism that I am worried about for Mojsov. I would take B040 up only if the GLP-1 attribution proved unworkable, and then with a citation limited to engineered T cells expressing costimulated CARs. I agree with your point on the B046 citation and kept the wording to physiology and active forms.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's priority for the active peptide is sound enough, relative to Habener's group, which I cannot verify from the supplied evidence. If it is not, my fallback is Holst and Drucker alone, not a Knudsen swap.
Whether the committee will accept a physiology-only citation that omits Knudsen, or will insist that drug development be credited.
Whether B040 without Eshhar, or B031 with PERK, ATF6 and integrated stress response work outside Mori and Walter, would be defensible attributions if B046 stalled.
statement.conflict_note: No change to my round-1 disclosure. I have co-authored with Sten Linnarsson (eight recorded works, not audited) and Jonas Frisen, neither of whom is a credited name on the shortlist. My single-cell and sequencing methods background is close to B024, which is not in my preferred configuration or alternatives this round. I have no documented link to any credited name on B046, B040 or B031 and see no need for recusal.
